utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, good morning, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I just wanted to clarify one procedural point arising out of the witness's evidence yesterday. I'd just like to ask him if he formally adopts his amalgamated statement as his evidence in that trial, which is a question which I omitted from the presentation yesterday. I've cleared this with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is it that we admitted as Exhibit P1830?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If that's the exhibit number for the amalgamated statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, that's the amalgamated statement of the witness. I simply wanted to ask him if he formally adopts it as his own evidence. It was simply that one sentence I left out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please do that, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday we discussed your amalgamated witness statement which you had an opportunity to review last week. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you if adopt that statement as your evidence, and if you were asked questions on those subjects, that you would provide the same answers if asked about those subjects today.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I adopt this statement as mine, and I would have answered every question posed in that statement in the same manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Miokovic. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Miokovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, did your government keep secret from the public incidents that involved massive casualties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, here it is: The incidents that involved massive civilian casualties, were those incidents publicised or was that concealed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every incident, as you call them, along the line of the police control and command, was reported in the proper manner as the police do. Whenever there were fatalities in these incidents, the department that I worked at at the time was notified, again by following proper procedure, and we would, in turn, inform that investigating judge. What followed was we would go to visit the site with or without the investigating judge to carry out on-site investigation, and every piece of information and detail would subsequently be forwarded to the investigating judge. This is all I can tell you with regards to this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's one side of the coin, but was that imparted on the public? Was that widely covered or was that concealed from the public?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sarajevo is a small town. That was particularly the case during the war. Anything of that nature, i.e., shooting from infantry or artillery weapons that resulted in one or more fatalities, would shortly after that become public without any specific publication. I'm not aware of a single incident that was in any way whatsoever hidden from the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With all due respect, I would kindly ask you to reduce as many answers as possible to a yes or a no answer, and I, in turn, would try to put as many questions to you and possibly without asking an extension of time. Yesterday, you said that you were involved in some hundred incidents' investigations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In another trial, you said a couple of hundred or several hundred. Which one of these figures is correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately not fewer than 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have the findings of yours relating to these investigations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that question. Everything I did, as I said, was done following a proper procedure and was submitted to the High Court in Sarajevo that existed at the time. That applied not only to me, but also to the entire team that worked on investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's a good answer. We'll ask for this from the OTP and then from the Bosnian Government. But the fact is that these documents relating to every single investigation do exist?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many of these investigations involved massive civilian casualties? Can you enumerate them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "massive civilian casualties," as far as police terminology is concerned, does not exist. Therefore, I don't know what you mean by "massive civilian casualties."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll try to be more precise. If, on the average, seven or eight casualties took place, everything above that could be called massive.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what is your question? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you list the incidents that you investigated that involved seven or eight or more civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot give you this information off the top of my head. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Out of these hundreds of investigations that you carried out, how many of them involved seven or more casualties? Can you tell that -- tell us that percentage-wise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than 10 or 15 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you give us some specific examples?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That would then involve 70 to 100 casualties. Now, where are the remaining 10.900 casualties who were involved?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I am the proper person to be asked that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't have asked you this hadn't you, yourself, given the figure of 11 casualties.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 11.000 casualties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Karadzic, I just provided an estimate that was prepared by the Sarajevo CSB, and as I said, to this date a large number of governmental and non-governmental organisations have confirmed this figure to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Approximately it's contradictio in adiecto. We're looking for an exact figure. Do you take it that, on the basis of this, there was 250.000 to 300.000 victims and that the total in Bosnia was 97.000?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I don't want to speculate on any figures relating to casualties. I really don't want to speculate and guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. This witness is not being presented as an expert witness in the field of demographics. There will be an expert witness in the field of demographics and total fatalities. Dr. Karadzic can direct his questions to the appropriate witness, when the appropriate witness arrives. This witness simply does not have that knowledge, and this, in my submission, is a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Mr. Karadzic, I think you exhausted this topic. Move on to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was seeking an explanation to the effect whether I am entitled to dispute everything that is being said by this witness. And if he's willing to withdraw this figure of 11.000, if is he prepared to do so, then I'm satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your right is not disputed. But it is of my opinion that the witness had given his answer as far as he could, so it's better for you to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, did you carry out investigations irrespective of the victim's ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many investigations did you carry out relating to murders of Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Serb victims who were killed by shelling or some other activity that came from the VRS lines or are you referring to the murders committed during the war but had nothing to do with the activities on the front-line?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the former is concerned, we in the police never kept record that would show the ethnicity of the victim because we didn't believe -- or, rather, the legislators didn't believe that was important. Now, as for your second question, I really cannot remember. I really cannot remember not even the identity of the victims that got killed outside of any shelling or sniping activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that the generals of your army, Caco and Juka Prazina and the others, were not killing Serbs around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said and as I confirmed, throughout the whole time I was in the police, Caco, as you call him, and Juka were never generals. And if you're asking me whether, during the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sarajevo, if there were any murders in Sarajevo simply because they were Serbs, yes, there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who investigated those cases?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sarajevo CSB, and probably the security services of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, that is something that I don't know anything about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in any of those investigations into the killings of Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bulk of these cases occurred during the 1992/1993 period, meaning at the very beginning, in the first year of the war. And I already said that I joined the CSB in December 1993, so I did not. But I am aware that a certain number of these cases was investigated and that a certain number of those cases was resolved, the perpetrators were prosecuted, and this applies to the wartime period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this refer to the victims who were thrown into Kazani? Did you hear of Kazani?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes, I have heard of Kazani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this referred to the victims of Kazani?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, this applies to the victims of Kazani -- actually, to the perpetrators of the deeds at Kazani, the crimes of murder committed at the Kazani locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how the situation relating to the Seve was resolved, and Nedzad Ugljen and Nedzad Herenda and Garaplija?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Miokovic. I'm wondering, Mr. Karadzic, how this is relevant to your case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Like this: We have a prominent investigator here who was investigating violent crimes or crimes in Sarajevo, and I'm going to state here -- I'm going to tell the witness here that the Serbian side in Sarajevo has names of 5.000 to 8.000 Serbs who disappeared in the town. This is a figure ranging between 5.000 to 8.000 Serbs, and this is something that was concealed by the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And this witness was in a position to investigate these particular cases, so I would like to see what he has to say about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While that may be important, my question is how that was relevant to your case. Probably, we allowed you too much time. I told you to prioritise your questions, and you cannot complain about a shortage of time while asking such irrelevant or marginally relevant issues. Come to your questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question for you to see that this relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, would you kindly explain to the Trial Chamber what the Seve are?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information, other than the fact -- or other than the things that I read about that in the media, and this is for a very simple reason. Seve, if they existed in the capacities that were published in the Bosnia and Herzegovina media, this was a unit that was part of the then Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I was never a member of that ministry. I was a member of the Sarajevo CSB. So I'm not able to provide any relevant information about that group to you or to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But if I were to tell you that Seves were the secret armed force of the Secret Police, which organised sniping of citizens in town and the killings of Serbs, and that finally the three of their founders, Nedzad Ugljen, Nedzad Herenda, were killed by that same police, and I don't know what happened to Garaplija. This is the information that I'm seeking from Bosnia-Herzegovina - you're an investigator - is it correct what I say, that Nedzad Ugljen and Nedzad Garaplija were killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with all due respect, I think you're getting things mixed up a little bit. Nedzad Ugljen was killed, Nedzad Garaplija is alive, and the other Nedzad is alive as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But they're in prison?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that this was an armed formatio of the Secret Police, of the Secret Service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was quite clear; I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, first of all, you're exploring matters that the witness has stated categorically that he can't answer. And so not only are you wasting your time, you're wasting everybody's time. Secondly, when you analyse what you're asking, you're often making a statement which is in the guise of a question. You simply make an interrogatory remark at the end of a long statement. That is not proper cross-examination. What you're doing is making submissions disguised as cross-examination, and the time will come for you to make proper submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, you said that a major obstacle to the investigations into the sniper incidents was created by the fact that the Serbs were using fragmentation ammunition. Can you please tell us what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that this posed an obstacle, but I do recall being asked, in a previous situation, the same question, and I remember stating that, during firing at trams - because in one of the cases that I investigated, this was the case - so-called fragmentation ammunition was used. I'm not a ballistics experts, so all I know about that is that this would be a fire-arm bullet, a rifle in this case, which, in contact with a certain surface, would burst into fragments, a number of fragments, and such a bullet can wound, injure, and kill more than one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the fifth page of your latest statement, fourth paragraph from the top, you say that it was customary for the army of the Bosnian Serbs to use fragmentation bullets. Do you know that this ammunition is banned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's banned, Dr. Karadzic, just as the siege of a town with a population of 400.000 is banned, but it still took place. I know fragmentation ammunition is banned. The use of cluster bombs is also banned, but it was still used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, thank you. Do you know that such ammunition does not exist for a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, with all due respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Both of you were overlapping. The interpreters couldn't follow. We stopped with the question whether -- Mr. Miokovic, whether you know that such ammunition does not exist for a rifle. Can you start from there again? What was your answer, Mr. Miokovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am not a ballistics expert. What I do know is that on several occasions -- on plenty of occasions during investigations into sniper fire at trams, in the investigation of such cases, I was told by technicians and ballistics experts, in an official manner at the scene, that in a specific case what was most probably used was fragmentation ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at your statement on page 5 and allow me that because your statement is admitted, I must dispute everything or I must attempt to prove everything. You did not say that in any conditional form. What remains in the statement will be admitted. Such ammunition does not exist. Such an ammunition must have an explosive charge; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So why did you say something that you don't know? Did you ever see us having obtained such ammunition? Did we ever obtain such ammunition? And can you please tell us, who manufactured such ammunition and such rifles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never interested in your procurements. And the second thing is, I'm saying this once again: What is stated in my official reports as for technical details among other things, that I put ammunition that was probably used, was something I was informed about by my colleagues, who were experts in that field, who were at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said a lot of things off the cuff, Mr. Miokovic, and now I have to cancel that out. Isn't it correct that you were quite approximate in the positions that you stated?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Please put a pause between the question and answer. The interpreters couldn't hear your answer, Mr. Miokovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that this is Dr. Karadzic's assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now focus on the incident of the 8th of November, 1994, in Livanjska Ulica. You were at that on-scene investigation? If possible can you please answer with yes or no, and I'm going to try to put my questions in that way.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first investigative judge in that incident was Milorad Potparic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At what time did you go to the scene?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer that question, I would kindly like to look at my official report on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we now look at 65 ter 09678. I think this is probably a P exhibit. This is 65 ter 09678.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's P1704. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's okay to publish the name. It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the report from this incident?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were informed at a quarter to 4.00. At what time did you actually go to the scene of the incident?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not specified in my report, so I can just estimate that this was perhaps at around 1610 hours. I really don't remember exactly anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about how early it got dark on the 8th of November in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question precisely, but I'm quite sure that, as far as that is concerned, the conditions were quite sufficient for us to be able to conduct our investigation on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then at 1640 hours, people from UNPROFOR turned up, military observers in one vehicle and other people from UNPROFOR in another vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you had a misunderstanding with them, and you prevented them from accessing the scene and participating in the inquiry?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question with a yes or no, in any case, because the answer, itself, if you wish to have an answer, requires me to elaborate. I cannot answer with a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Then after talking with them -- you can look at your statement. This is page 8, and I think this is in the previous statement, where you say that after 1640 hours, you began your investigation activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that on the screen, Dr. Karadzic. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the third page of your previous statement. The ERN number --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What page, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page -- ERN 0305-9529. This is the ERN number of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This statement has been incorporated into the amalgamated statement, so essentially Mr. Karadzic is referring to page 3 of the amalgamated statement. It's the same evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's formulated a little bit differently here, so the previous statement is a bit more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you completed your conversation with them at 1640 hours and you started the investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We began the investigation even before the military observers and the UNPROFOR members came to the scene. It's been a long time since then, so I'm unable to remember the precise time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you were asked about this in other cases, but now I'm going to read that paragraph: "I came back to the scene, and one of my people told me that Major Iki" something - from Kenya, probably - "tried to pull out a shell from the ground, but it was so firmly stuck in the ground that it could not be moved. My men warned him not to do that. Then we began the investigation." According to this statement, you began the investigation at 1640 hours.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that event and what I stated. What I'm absolutely sure about, and it's very simple to establish that by looking at the video footage which is part of this official report, is that even before the UNMOs and the UNPROFOR soldiers came, we began the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you came to the scene after 4.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you finished at 1655 hours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in my statements, but I repeat, once again, that I cannot, after such a long time, confirm the exact timeline.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me whether you invited them to participate, or did you prevent them from attending and participating in the investigation, themselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two military observers first came to the scene, and they were immediately told -- it was explained to them what this was all about very quickly. After them, the two combat vehicles, as far as I can remember, came to the scene which were usually used by members of the French UNPROFOR battalion. One soldier, in full combat kit, came out of the vehicle, together with an interpreter, and he set off towards the scene of the incident. I note that in this event, one little girl was killed on the spot. A number of persons were wounded, some of whom died later. There was a certain number of people there, citizens. I mean, simply, the atmosphere there at the scene was very tense because of everything that had happened and because of the fact that throughout that whole time, the shelling of the town was going on. This French soldier who started to move towards the location was a little bit unusual. I stepped in front of him and asked him, through his interpreter, what does he want, why was he going there. This was not the usual way in which UNPROFOR soldiers that worked on investigations together with us behaved. He said that he just came to see the scene, and I warned him that the atmosphere was what it was and that there is no problem, that they can do the investigation together with us, but we would need to follow the usual procedures. He called somebody on the radio, spoke with them, and immediately -- actually, before that, he said that they were very quickly going to come to the scene. Then he got into his vehicle, and then he left. Immediately after he -- after those soldiers left, the scene -- the military observers also left the scene who were informed about all the relevant information that we had had up until that time at the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You acted as the leader of the on-site investigation team; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, had this gentleman behaved differently, you would allow them to attend the on-site investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His intention was never to attend the on-site investigation. That's not why he was there. Was that the reason why he had come there, he would have done it, but his reasons were elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What were his reasons, Mr. Miokovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he just said, I came to see what was going on. I told him what was going on. Then he exchanged a few words with someone, and he said, Very soon our team will come as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A few moments ago, you said that his conduct was the reason why you prevented him from attending the scene, the crime scene. Was the conduct, his conduct, the reason -- and you said it wasn't fair. Was that the reason why you didn't let him attend the scene?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say "his conduct," I said "his body language." For instance, the way he carried his rifle, I assessed and I was quite certain that he was not a member of an investigation team. His bearing was military, and in the situation in which I found myself, I judged that such a conduct of his could be -- could jeopardise both him and his men, as well as the investigation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, had he not been armed, your position would have been different; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were always armed. But it's one thing to have your rifle on your shoulder and the other thing is to have it -- to hold it in your hands almost cocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that before that incident, you had taken the position - when I say "you," I mean investigators - that UNPROFOR should not be allowed to attend the on-site investigations and that they should not be allowed to conduct an investigation before you had a chance to do it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who convened the meeting where this position was taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall who it was, exactly. It was probably some -- an authorised person. But that meeting was convened at our prompting, the investigators' prompting, the investigator in the Violent Crimes Department of the Sarajevo CSB, the persons who normally conducted this type of on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of your amalgamated statement, you say that it was standard practice within the centre for investigative procedures -- [In English] "It had been a practice for UNPROFOR, who were more mobile and better organised up until then, to get to the scene before us. Then they then took the trace, such as shell fragments, which were then vital to our investigation. After taking the traces of evidence, they would issue a report that we were not able to challenge." [Interpretation] Was it possible to check and repeat every on-site investigation? And I mean reconstruct it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What type of investigation do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, every on-site investigation that was conducted was properly documented. What do you mean, was it possible to check them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, what was it that prompted you on this occasion to issue an order to the effect that no one should be allowed to attend the scene, and especially so where UNPROFOR members were concerned? What kind of experiences that you previously had prompted you to do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's leave Bosnia and Herzegovina aside. What was it that prompted you not to allow UNPROFOR to attend on-site investigations that you conducted, that you -- what were the -- what was your past experience with them that prompted you to take such a decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the main task --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please refrain from giving us lectures here. Just tell us why you -- what prompted you and what made you take such conclusions.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are very serious questions, and the way they are being put to me, I'm not capable to answer them. This is a very serious question. However, I cannot answer in just one or two sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, you're the author of your own misfortune. You asked for yes-and-no answers, and then you ask questions which patently cannot be answered simply yes or no. And you are also tending to engage in argument with the witness, which is not -- again, not a proper form of cross-examination. You've got to think about these things more carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, that's quite all right. I was simply saying that Mr. Karadzic claimed that the witness was giving us lectures. The witness has not been giving us lectures at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, I accept the Trial Chamber's -- I will accept the Trial Chamber's instructions. I will try to be more specific, and, please, would you also be more specific in your answers. Now, was this conclusion or this position taken at someone's initiative at this meeting of all police investigators in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a conclusion or a position taken exclusively on the basis of the needs of our service, because it was our responsibility under the law to collect all relevant material evidence. Now, in practice, there were frequent instances where UNPROFOR, precisely for the reasons that you quoted that I mentioned in my statement, actually reaches the site before us, collects all that evidence, and then, once we arrive there in order to conduct an on-site investigation, there was no more trace evidence there. And I would like to stress here, again, we at the CSB, the Sarajevo CSB, did not attend UNPROFOR on-site investigations. It was our legal obligation to document each incident, and it was the free -- it was at the UNPROFOR's will to actually assess whether they want to check it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Miokovic, now, you say in your statement that UNPROFOR would issue a report that then you could not contest; in other words, you were bothered by their investigative practices. Now, could you please tell us what it was that bothered you? What practices or what techniques did the UNPROFOR implement that you object to, that led you to act as you did? Could you give us some example?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, in practice, there were instances where UNPROFOR, either publicly or addressing themselves to the officials of Bosnia and Herzegovina, would put forth some statements that had to do with one of the incidents, either shelling or sniping, and where their findings were not consistent with what our findings were. In order to avoid misunderstandings and to come to the -- I can't really say "absolute truth," but to try to establish the truth to the best of our abilities about a certain incident, the only thing that we insisted on was to be able to conduct an on-site investigation in a fair manner and in keeping with the usual practices within our profession, and that is why we demanded that no investigation be conducted until our investigative team came to the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, did the investigation in Livanjska Street -- was it a representative sample of your service's way of conducting an investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think this is a representative sample for a simple reason: The circumstances in which we conducted this on-site investigation were really impossible, even for Sarajevo, but we did try to follow the procedure that was the standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, what would your objections be to this on-site investigation, or, rather, to this report? What is it that is missing from it, regardless of what the reasons were? Or, rather, what is missing from this on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really see that there's anything missing in this official report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, it is a representative sample. If we are able to explore this one thoroughly, then that would be tantamount to having explored all the other ones?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really say that. I can't say that in wartime conditions you could say that there is a representative sample.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did the investigating judge authorise you to be the team leader, and did he issue a written statement to that effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Written decisions are not normally issued, and that's not something that is normal procedure, but he did authorise me to conduct this on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In doing so, did he know that you did not -- that you do not have a college -- university degree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, he thought that you do have -- did have a college degree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was not an illegal police employee. I had been a police officer for many years up until then, and I believe that Mr. Potparic perhaps didn't even know whom he was talking to, I mean, personally. He was the investigating judge, and I was the police officer at the scene, and he was the person issuing orders that I had to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, on page 16, lines 2 and 3 -- well, let me ask you this before: What was the purpose of conducting the Livanjska Street investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, was it conducted in order to bring the perpetrators to court?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was our deep conviction -- or at least it was our deep desire to see all and each and every one of our on-site investigation reports reviewed before a court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, your answer is, yes, you conducted this investigation in the effort to have the perpetrators brought to justice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, on page 16, on top, you said that investigating judges always attended on-site investigations, that was the case then, whereas today it would be the prosecutor, and then there would also be a police officer conducting an investigation who would have a university degree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, either you did not understand what I said or you're misquoting here. You should make a difference between an investigation and a forensic on-site investigation. A forensic on-site investigation is only a portion of the overall investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, was this on-site investigation irrelevant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not. It was very important. In this case, it was even crucial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I think Mr. Karadzic has, in fact, misquoted the evidence. And just for the record, I want to quote the question and answer. The question was: "When we talk about the crime of murder, is it important for the Court that the investigation was conducted by an investigating judge? "A. At that time, that was an investigating judge. Nowadays, it's a prosecutor." And he goes on with his answer. The reason I raise it now is because this is not the first time Mr. Karadzic has blatantly misquoted the evidence -- the prior evidence of a witness during cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm telling you, Mr. Karadzic, for the third time, come to your specific questions about this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, on page 3, you go on to say that it was standard procedure to determine the direction from which the shell came; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was established by my colleagues, ballistics expert, who attended the crime scene together with the forensic technicians, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What method was used to establish that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a ballistics expert, and I don't know what method was used to establish that, in general, let alone in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this particular case, did your conclusion differ again from UNPROFOR's?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous answer, I tried to explain how the whole thing proceeded vis-a-vis UNPROFOR in this particular case. So speaking of the 8th of November, after the on-site investigation was carried out, as far as I know, UNPROFOR did not have any information about this incident other than what we had forwarded to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to refer you to the first page of your on-site investigation report, where you mention six individuals who participated in this investigation under your leadership. Which of these individuals is a ballistics expert?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirza Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did he submit a report in which he determined the direction of the shell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to what he did on the spot?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, did you compile your report based on that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, with all due respect, are we talking about this official report that I see in front of me on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the first one you submitted on the 8th of November. You submitted it the very same day.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand what you mean. The procedure is as follows --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please -- do not try to educate us on that. Did you submit this report on the very same day, at the request of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is not a proper statement. Once you ask the question, let the witness -- the witness is entitled to answer in what form he wants to answer. That's what you wanted to say, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's quite right, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And often you overlap. On your part, put a pause between the answer and the question. And we'll come to the question of -- you referred to Mr. Sabljica's report, and you come to the question abruptly as to the date of his submission of statement. What was your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Miokovic was asked about -- actually, he asked which report I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I'm asking you: Is it true or not that you, on the same day, at the request of the Presidency, submitted your report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, you are again mixing up things. What you see on the screen is my official report. It was my duty -- it was incumbent upon me that as soon as I get back to my office from any on-site investigation, to draft this official report containing all this information that you can see here, including the technical details that were provided to me by the ballistic expert and the criminal investigation technicians as preliminary information. This official report is only one integral part of the case file that, after the ballistics expert and forensic technicians do their work, was submitted to the judge. This official report of mine was never submitted to the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, nor was it compiled with that purpose in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In -- I'm sorry, I have to -- in your statement, you said that at 2000 hours on that same day, the UNPROFOR spokesman - that's paragraph 3 - said at the press conference that the Bosnian police had not allowed them to carry out an investigation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be present during the investigation, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To conduct an investigation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then on the same page, you said that you had ordered the investigation to be finalised by 1730, but that the next shell came at 5.20?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Can you please be more specific? What do you want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you have your statement in front of you? Do we have a B/C/S version of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, the amalgamated statement is just in English. There should be a B/C/S version of the original statement. I'll try to find that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you'd like to put your question, Mr. Karadzic, give an exact citation and put the question accordingly. What your statement says is like this, Mr. Miokovic. For your information, I will read it out: "On that same day, on a press conference held by UNPROFOR at 8.00 p.m. that evening, a spokesman said to the journalist that Bosnian police had not allowed them to carry out an investigation. On that same evening, our minister of interior passed an order to prepare the report because it was requested by the presidency of the state, and I did." So that's what you said in your statement, and Mr. Karadzic asked about -- asked whether it was done by the request of the Presidency. That was the question. Can you answer the question again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This official report, which is in front of me at the moment, is a single document. When, at 2000 hours, the UNPROFOR announced everything that was said, I was informed by my superiors everything that you already quoted. The minister was interested to know what happened with our communication with UNPROFOR and whether it was true that UNPROFOR did not attend the investigation. Of course, I sent a separate report on those questions to the minister. He, or the Presidency, were not interested at all in the data that is in the document in front of me. I prepared this document, and I described how things happened, and I passed this on to the minister through proper channels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Miokovic. Don't argue with the witness. Put your questions one by one. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you ordered the investigation to be finalised by 5.30, and that at 5.25 another shell fell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After UNPROFOR departed, I waited for about 10 minutes after the completion of our investigation, expecting them to come and for me to give them information that they would require. Since they failed to appear, and the shelling was in progress, I issued an order for all the relevant clues and evidence to be collected from the spot and that we remove ourselves from the scene. What I can assert with full responsibility, at 5.25, when, at about 20 or 50 metres from the investigation site, another shell fell, my investigation team was not on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that the reason why you conducted this investigation in such a hasty manner, the reason that you cited was that there were shells falling in the general area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that we conducted our investigation under such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the next shell fell only at 5.25; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that the term "only" is an appropriate one when you speak about shells. Had my team been there on the spot when the shell fell only at 2.25 [as interpreted], I cannot imagine what the consequences would be, but I believe that both I and my team would be in direct danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are we then to take it that while you were on the spot after 5.00, no shells fell in your vicinity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in this micro-area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you say that the initial finding of the French UNPROFOR of the 9th of November, 1994, specified that the shell was fired from the position of BH Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only attended this investigation, and I say "attended" because the investigating judge was there at the time. What I do remember is that the ballistic experts from the CSB and the republican ministry conducted their separate investigations, whereas members of the French Battalion did their investigations. Their findings concerning the origin of fire of the shell were identical. However, there was a dilemma whether the shell had been fired from the positions of BH Army or the Republika Srpska Army, and UNPROFOR's argument was that the charge of the shell was insufficient for it to arrive at the spot had it been fired by the VRS. In order to corroborate that, they provided information from Finnish tables, I believe, to which our ballistic expert provided them with another table that had been used by the Yugoslav People's Army, and that there was some discrepancy in the charges. The Finnish tables did not take into account the charges that existed in the shells used by the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that later. Is it true that on the 9th this case was taken over by another investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another investigating judge became involved primarily in order to conduct an investigation on the second and third shells that fell on the 8th, the one at 5.25 and 5.30. Because members of the UNPROFOR were already there, wishing to investigate the first shell that fell at 5.30, but I'm not sure about the times any longer, then the investigating judge instructed our team to join in into this reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the investigating judge for the first shell was a Serb, Milorad Potparic, whereas the investigating judge for the other two shells was a Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me quote the words of Mr. Sabljica, who is stated as a ballistic expert in your report. It's document 20874, 65 ter, page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1735, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please focus on paragraph 7, where it reads: "I saw these were Finnish mortar tables. He explained that they used the maximum charge for their calculations. When comparing it to our tables, we saw that the maximum tables of the Finnish tables correspond with the second or the third charge indicated in our tables, in which we have six possible charges. Then we showed them our tables, which were original JNA documents, which indicate --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please indicate the second part that he's reading from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what kind of answer you're expecting me to give. Your Honours, I honestly don't understand. I absolutely don't understand what I am being asked, and I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not recorded in the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just put a pause. Your question was not noted by the interpreter, so that we couldn't understand what your question was. What was your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is what Mr. Sabljica stated in this statement? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How can he know what Mr. Sabljica stated or not? What is your question? This is Mr. Sabljica's statement, and what is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Excellency, Mr. Miokovic was a team leader. He was responsible for this investigation in every respect. Sabljica was his co-worker. He, himself, mentioned the Finnish tables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Karadzic, to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, the third and particularly the second charge, according to the JNA tables, indicate that the shell had been fired from the territory of BH Army, and that was something that you took an issue with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the time when this on-site investigation was carried out, I was not the team leader. The investigating judge, Izet Bazdarevic, was the team leader. Never had I in any way whatsoever got myself directly involved in any technical discussions conducted by experts. I still don't know what is the difference between the second and the third charge of mortar shells, neither according to the Finnish or to the tables of the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D02264. 1D02264.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D738, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the report, the technical report; is that correct? Are you familiar with this map and this diagram, this drawing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I'm seeing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see that, according to their tables, a shell has eight charges and not four, as stated by your ballistics expert?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect, I really don't want to go into the merits of the technical portion of the report, because I'm not qualified to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you are simply wasting your time. We heard the witness's answer, that he was not in the position to answer these technical questions. Was that your point, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is concerned about your way of putting your questions, in particular today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, like this, Your Excellency: This witness said that the conflict -- or the misunderstanding between them and the UNPROFOR investigation team was in the Finnish tables, and that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The dispute was about the point of firing, isn't that right, that the UNPROFOR concluded that this was fired from the territory under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Yes or no. That was their conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was that a question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the dispute, or, rather, the misunderstanding between your team and the UNPROFOR team relating to the place of firing, and they claim that this was fired from the territory that was under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the decision was made to use one set of tables or the other. But, still, this was a conversation between the technical part of the team. I listened to this conversation, but did not take part in any element of that conversation, so I don't know what the official conclusion of UNPROFOR is on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know whether they accepted your suggestions or not. Do you know that what you're talking about, this difference in the tables, is not true and that they actually used Yugoslav tables; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, do you know that they made a comparison of the values of the tables, and that you did not convince them that it was what you were saying; that they stayed by their own findings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that, and I'm repeating it again. Thus, even now, when you and I are talking, I don't know what the definitive conclusion of UNPROFOR was in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Miokovic, this is what it says on page 4 in your -- that you -- after the investigation, you went to the premises, and that you looked over the findings, that you established -- you said that they had used Finnish tables, that they showed you something else, and that you saw their report here in 2007 in court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to have on the screen all of the things that you have just mentioned so that I can remind myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 14 of your statement. In response to a question: [In English] "I remember that the UNPROFOR carried out some measurements there, and that they conducted an on-site investigation. I also know that it was a common practice then in such situation." [Interpretation] Then you go on to say that: [In English] "All these named parameters coincided. With regard of the position of UNPROFOR in relation to local police, I am referring exclusively to the city of Sarajevo. Mind you, UNPROFOR was not obliged to officially inform police of their findings. Yesterday or the day before yesterday - correct me if I'm wrong - I saw UNPROFOR's official report about this on-site investigation about these two mortar shells for the first time." [Interpretation] So it's not new to you now. You said a little bit earlier that you'd never seen it, you don't know what their conclusion was, but at the trial of General Milosevic, you did see that report, and you did see that there is a difference there from your report.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask you again, if possible, for me to have what you have allegedly now quoted and what have you in front of you. I stand by every word in every proceedings that I have been in, but in this way I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, the problem is that there is no amalgamated statement of yours in the Serbian. But this is page 14, so I would like the Prosecution to help their witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you bring that up, Exhibit P1830, page 14.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From line 23 to 35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, do you read English? Is it okay? So shall I read it so you can hear the interpretation or you can read your statement in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is sufficient, Your Honours. I just need a little bit of time to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is written here stands, with the proviso that from this context, I'm really unable to tell what I meant when I said "UNPROFOR report," whether that was what was published in the media, because at this point I really don't recall that I saw an official report of UNPROFOR on this event. I don't remember reading it carefully and checking it. And in the end, for me, professionally, in this situation the position of UNPROFOR was not a decisive matter, as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they have smaller professional capacities than your team?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I doubt that. Quite the contrary, I believe that they did have the capacity and, I assume, also the personnel that was capable of performing the job properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And their conclusion was that the shell came in from the territory under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that conclusion of theirs, Dr. Karadzic. I really don't see it. I don't know whether they officially confirmed, wrote, and signed what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what was the disagreement between UNPROFOR and your team, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, if Dr. Karadzic is going to keep referring to this report, it's already in evidence at D738. The conclusion of the UNPROFOR team is at the third page of that report. And in my submission, it's already in evidence, Your Honours have it, they have the Bosnian reports as well, and they have all the relevant evidence relating to this incident, and Your Honours can consider that at the opportune moment. This cross-examination is going well beyond this witness's participation in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree. It's time to take a break for 20 minutes, and we'll move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for allowing me to address you. I have to state that this case is a blatant case of all the things that happened in Sarajevo. What happened here is that they changed the direction of the first shell and did not allow UNPROFOR to investigate the case. They moved the direction or the axis of the direction from which the shell had come. They did not have time to do the same with the second shell, and the UNPROFOR then concluded that it had come from the Muslim side. So that's number 1. They had not allowed UNPROFOR to attend the site on the first day, and then they tried to say that the Kenyan member of the UNPROFOR had tried to manipulate this. Now, I would like to have an additional 10 minutes to show how this all happened there and how it was done, and all the things that are being imputed to me, which is why I'm sitting here as the accused. That's very simple. He has to know this because he was the person who took the photographs away. If he's not a ballistics expert, okay, but these things he must be aware of because he was the one who did these things. And I do admit that I'm not being very efficient today, but this is because of the witness, who is refusing to answer properly or directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Karadzic, it would be a brave man who said that he was efficient every day. We realise very much the direction in which you wish to go in this. You will understand that we've all been in this business for many years. It isn't the relevance of the central thrust of your cross-examination that's the problem. It's been the way in which it was conducted. If you have a direct point to make to the witness concerning the issues that you've just raised in the last few minutes, then put them directly to the witness, as direct questions, and see what the response is. We're not trying to stop you cross-examining. What we're trying to do is make it more focused, and that's really for two reasons: First, to make it more time efficient, and, secondly, to make sure that you get out of the cross-examination that which you need to get out of it. That mustn't be seen, as it were, as any bias towards you. But we well recognise that you are not a professional lawyer and the Prosecution lawyers are professional lawyers, and so, to a degree, there is latitude being given to you to take that into account. But it can only be to a degree. There cannot be an unreservedly open account in respect of either time or methodology. It may be, and this is something -- I'm speaking entirely for myself now, this is not something that the Trial Chamber has discussed in the absence -- in our short absence recently, but I'm just speaking for myself. It's something I'm thinking aloud, in essence. It may be that without, in any sense, giving up your right to self-representation, that there are some witnesses that you would feel it better to delegate cross-examination to a professional lawyer. I don't expect a response from you instantly on that, but I think it's something you ought to think about, because we've got a long road ahead of us, and the easier it's made is going to be beneficial for all parties.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apologies for your inconvenience, Mr. Miokovic. We had something to discuss in your absence. So we'll open the curtain again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, we will briefly now touch upon some matters that you must have been the one who conducted them. Is this procedure of collecting evidence, and especially specifically photo documentation, was that your job?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in the professional sense. But technically speaking, that was the work of the forensic technicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is now for you to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Kenyan UNPROFOR officer tried to recover the fins -- the tail-fin of the first shell, because that is what you stated in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I don't know why Mr. Karadzic keeps referring to this officer as Kenyan. The evidence was there was one major from Nigeria and one from Bangladesh. There are no Kenyan personnel involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we all understood.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My error. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did an UNPROFOR officer, wherever he may have been from, try to recover the tail-fin of the first shell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone try to recover the tail-fin of the second shell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 20879, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1702, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this sketch? Is this part of the investigative file?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that with certainty because, from what I see on the monitor, I cannot really infer from that that this sketch actually relates to this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it is from the same file, but never mind. Can we then briefly just hear this from you: Did you take the photo documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this on-site investigation also had video documentation, in part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you accept that this sketch is part of your report? I mean, will you take it from me or do I need to prove that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, I would rather not rely on what you're saying. But if you show me the number or the evidence -- or exhibit number, I will then be able to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you. Then let's take a look at the video excerpt, and then we will see whether this was part of the on-site investigation report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, here we see that -- on the sketch that we saw earlier, we saw that the angle -- the incoming angle was 67 degrees; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 66.96, that's the angle alpha, if that's what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Can you see the time shown here? It says "1630 hours."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please watch this carefully. The next moment, we will see that it shows "1631." Can we now please play this video?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you discern the angle of this stabiliser or tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from this photo, I can just conclude that there is a part called a stabiliser, a tail-fin, but that's all I can conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But isn't the angle almost perpendicular, 90 degrees?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection. The witness has said several times that he's not an expert in ballistics. That was the role of other members of the team. This is venturing clearly into the area of ballistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the witness would be able to answer the question from this video-clip. I tend to agree with Mr. Gaynor's observation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I won't ask him about the angle. What I want to know is whether the position of this stabiliser, whether it had been altered. Now, please, I would like to ask you all to bear in mind this photo and the position of this tail-fin, and then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did this person, or, rather, was this video edited in any way or was it just one video excerpt in continuity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this video was taken on-site and it was in sequences. In other words, it did not cover the entire on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, let's move on. So we see it's "1631" here. Let's move on. Let's play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you see that there was some intervention here -- that there was some editing done here on the video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really understand your question, or your claim.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's play it again, and then you will see that there is a cut there. So this was not actually taped in continuity, there was a cut, but let's play it over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we see the moment; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which moment exactly you're referring to. I don't understand what you're trying to tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2675, please. 1D2675.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the photo on the left-hand side is a still from the video that we saw a moment ago? Or, rather, I apologise. The still on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, the one on the right-hand side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you see that on the left-hand side, we can see the same tail-fin stabiliser which is a bit differently placed and that the angle is smaller?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with all due respect, what you're asking me to do is to speak about things that I am not an expert on. And in view of the fact that I'm not an expert on this, I really cannot observe this difference that you can, comparing these photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, we see a measuring stick, and that was placed there by your team. Now, we can see that this is the same exact impact site. Now, is this curve that we see here, was that -- and this different angle, is that the result of somebody pulling out the stabiliser or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the only way I can answer your question is this: Fully aware of the fact that I am under oath as I testify here, I state with full responsibility that any manipulation for the purpose of altering the crime scene or falsifying the evidence, no such manipulation was done here, and I stand by what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But can you see that the -- where we see that the asphalt or the pavement is cracked, that it's exactly the same and that the angle at which the stabiliser lies is now a bit different?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all the features of both of these photographs, I assume -- or, rather, I think that it is the same impact site and the same shell. The differences that you're referring to, or the similarities, I really cannot comment in any way, in view of the fact how the photographs are taken and whether they're close up or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2676, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
