utterances.text: Before we move on: Mr. Miokovic, do you not agree that in order to say there must have been some alteration or not you have to see the same picture from the same angle? These two pictures were taken from a different angle. The picture on the right side is a picture seen from the left side of the left photo. It's very difficult to tell there's -- the angle of descent is the same or not from these pictures.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully agree with what you said. Naturally, I have my own opinion about this. However, given that I'm not an expert in ballistics, I really don't want to intentionally try to make some speculations and things like that. I am quite sure that the Court has -- can bring people who would be fully qualified to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that the next photograph is going to show exactly what your question was about, so I would like to call up 1D2676, and eventually we're going to tender these photographs into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, do you agree that here we have two frames from the video and we have your photograph here? Let's forget about the angles and the ballistics. Let's just concentrate on what we can see with the naked eye. Do these two positions, one on the film and one on the photograph, differ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, upon arrival on the site, as always, and in this specific case as well, the first thing to be done was to film and photograph the position of the fragment of a projectile embedded in the asphalt, and this is what one can see in these two film frames. As for the photograph where you can see the stick in position, it means that in the meantime the criminal investigation technicians have cleared the area around the mortar shell, itself, in order to enable them to physically position a benchmark according to which, in the further proceedings, the angle of descent of the mortar would be determined, and this is a difference between the situation shown in these two frames as opposed to the situation in the photograph underneath. So there is no dispute that before the photo was taken with regard to these frames, the crime-of-scene officer approached the shell in order to clear the space around it for the stick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's leave aside the issue of angle. It couldn't be less than 80, but let's forget about that. Somebody tried to pull out this shell, and its position was altered. The position of the second shell was not changed, for which the UNPROFOR decided it came from your position. As for the first one, whose position had been altered, it was determined that it came from the Serbian positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are again making assertions that you expect me to confirm and to take your word for that. I don't want and I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's move now to the next incident. But before that, can we have these photographs admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's deal with them one by one. Do you tender that video-clip?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we have the 65 ter number? Is it 40574?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, 40574 is the entire video. It's about four minutes long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, so we have to identify that time portion, but we didn't. We'll admit that portion which was shown to the witness, and the time slot will be identified by the Defence, to be conveyed to the Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The entire video has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video is Exhibit P1849, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you identify the time slot for the record later on. And then we -- and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And about the photo analysis, do you have any objection, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would like -- I would like to note that this photo compilation has been prepared by the Defence team for Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With that caveat, we'll admit both of them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D2675 will be Exhibit D844, and 1D2676 will be Exhibit D845.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you investigate the sniping incident number 16 from the F list, the one that took place on the 3rd of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember taking part in that, but I would kindly ask for my official report relative to this incident to be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, can we have 65 ter 10439, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In addition to this report that you made, was there another Sarajevo MUP report produced?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it this is P1727.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that I made this official report. But whether there were any other reports, I am not able to tell you at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that we see your names here -- your name here and that you were designated the chief inspector here, because you are number 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used to call that the team leader for a specific on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in this instance, that was you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who set up the team and who appointed you the leader?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Are we looking at the same document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation refers to another report that I made reference to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's coming. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did Judge Potparic set up a team and appointed you the leader?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigating judge is not the one who set up a team. There is an obligation to notify the investigating judge from the relevant department. In this instance, I informed the judge, and he, in turn, appointed me the leader of the investigation team. After that, through proper channels of information, I informed my fellow workers from the Criminal Investigation Ballistics Section to join me in this investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any written order or authorisation issued in this case to the effect that you would be the team leader?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, in such situations no written authorities were envisaged by the law. Consequently, no authorisations of that nature were issued at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So according to the law, the judge does not issue or write any orders under the law?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Orders relating to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: An order relating to the investigation and the forming of the team and the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such provision in the law. In practice, both during the war and in peacetime, I have never received a written order from an investigating judge back then or from the prosecutor nowadays to conduct an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have to wait for the interpretation to finish. Did Judge Potparic, himself, visit the scene of crime, and did he lead the investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my official report of 3rd March 1995, it is stated that Judge Potparic led the team, visited the site, and conducted on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he was the one who commenced it and finalised it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was standard practice for a judge to both commence and complete the on-site investigation once he is present there. I cannot remember any extraordinary occurrence that would remove him from the spot. After so many years, I cannot confirm that he was there all the time, but I suppose he was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 10439.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Mihajlo Pavlovic is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, at the time Colleague Pavlovic was, I believe, an operative in the Centar Police Station, which in hierarchal terms is one step below the CSB.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have page 5 of this document, page 5 in both the Serbian and the English, or the previous page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a report compiled by another investigating team led by Mihajlo Pavlovic, but your name is also mentioned here as a member of the team?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it possible that I have this report in my own language? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in paragraph 2 it says: "The duty investigating judge of the Sarajevo High Court was notified ..." And then added by hand, "Milorad Potparic, who formed an inquiry commission consisting of ..." The composition is pretty similar. We have "Mihajlo Pavlovic," number 1, and number 2, we see "Dragan Miokovic"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see from your report that this incident took place where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have my report on the monitor, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's first see, according to this report, where this incident occurred. Can you say specifically at which intersection this happened, according to the report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see here is that the tram was moving from Cengic Vila towards Bascarsija. If you can help me find exactly where the location is specified. The tram was at the intersection of Zmaja od Bosne and Franje Rackog.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So according to you, this happened at this intersection between Zmaja od Bosne and Franje Rackog Street; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the previous page, or, rather, the next page, in which we see Mr. Miokovic's name first on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Below the names, is there anywhere where you can determine where this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to this paragraph which starts: "Upon arrival at the scene at the tram stop Marin Dvor ..." Yes, I hereby confirm that the on-site investigation was carried out at tram stop Marin Dvor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the difference between these two locations between 200 and 300 metres?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a difference. But I would like to say and underline that in my colleague Mihajlovic's [as interpreted] report, he specifically indicated the place where allegedly the tram was fired on. But in my report, I specify the position of the tram, itself, and the place where the on-site investigation was conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It says the examination of the scene happened in the presence of the Higher Court judge, Mico Potparic; operative of the CSB, Dragan Miokovic; and Mirza Sabljica; and Criminal Investigator Sasa Kurto; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the report in front of me, but that's probably what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what does it say in your report about that? Let's take a look. Can we look at the next page of this report, please. So you carried out the investigation at a distance of 200 to 300 metres away from the alleged impact point of the bullet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say -- can we look at page 2 so that we can see whether the judge carried out the investigation. The investigative judge was informed about this, and then it says that the investigating judge heard that an UNPROFOR soldier was hit, and that he abandoned the on-scene investigation relating to this event.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We don't know where the accused is reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that correct? The one paragraph but last. So the investigating judge abandoned an investigation into this case: "UNPROFOR personnel also carried out an investigation on the site"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. This document that you are quoting is a dispatch, it's a telegram, simply put, in order to convey information internally within the CSB. Judge Potparic abandoned the investigation at the scene, or establishing the facts at the scene relating to the fact that an UNPROFOR member was hit, because somebody from the command personnel of the FrenchBat that was there did not permit the investigating judge to conduct an investigation. So the fact that the judge abandoned the investigation relates to the information that an UNPROFOR soldier was hit. It does not imply a suspension of the investigation which related to the original event or incident due to which we came to the scene.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D02545, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that one of the victims and a witness here, Alen Gicevic, stated in a statement that he was hit at a tram station at Marin Dvor, the one facing the factory, the tobacco factory, once the tram had passed the Executive Council building? This is not this one. 1D02545, or, rather, 1D02545. Are you aware that Gicevic gave a statement the first time that he was hit after the tram had passed the Executive Council building, somewhere along the stretch of the tobacco factory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that detail after so much time has passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see here -- can we have the Serbian version that Mr. Miokovic -- so that Mr. Miokovic can see what Gicevic said. And this was later corrected, but the first statement was that the impact point was at the place where you inspected the tram. Can we look at the Serbian version of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What part of this document do you like the witness to take a look?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to look at the Serbian version, because I can find my way around that much more easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm advised that there's no B/C/S version for this information sheet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then we are going to call up the photograph so it can help us to locate or situate this incident. Well, can we then have the map while we're waiting for the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You may bear in mind what Judge Morrison told you a moment ago. The witness said he cannot remember that detail after so much time has passed, and there's no point to put similar questions to the witness. Just put your case to the witness and hear what he says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but we need to situate where the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you -- did your team establish the angle of the incoming bullet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this information has been noted down as a preliminary piece of information in my report, or, rather, if within the dossier there is relevant documentation that has to do with that particular segment of the inquiry, then I am able to answer that question for you. But like this, just going by my memory, I really cannot recall that particular detail in relation to that case. I cannot speak with any authority about that. It's a question of whether this was established or not established, and I'm sure that this is something that was documented in the report by the ballistics expert.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at page 19 of this 10439. Page 19, 10439, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read while we are reading that: "The mouth of the fire-arm at the moment that the bullet was fired was on the left side of the tram, behind the tram; namely, the direction of fire was in relation to the right-hand side of the tram from the back towards the front, from the right towards the left, and from the top down. The angle of the trajectory of the bullet in relation to the right side of the tram was 80 degrees."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Is this the report signed by Zlatko Medjedovic, because I can see that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see what you have read out, the last paragraph. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you locate the correct English page for this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here "Report from the Criminal --" now we're going to look and see where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph: "The mouth of the fire weapon ..." Is that what it says here, "the muzzle."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you are putting this question to me, then, yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I can't find the similar passage in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last paragraph, the last paragraph of this page 0331-6379, the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm asking the English page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the English version on the right-hand side of the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's page 19 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it says here that the angle of the trajectory, in relation to the right side of the tram, is 80 degrees, and the angle of the bullet trajectory, in relation to the floor, is 4 degrees?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would that be an almost vertical strike, almost at the right angle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot comment on this, in view of the fact that the angle of the bullet trajectory, in relation to the ground, is something that I really don't know anything about. I am not a ballistics expert. I don't see a connection between these two pieces of information, this 80-degree angle and 4-degree angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think it's page 9 in the English. Can the participants please pay attention to the top part of the page on the right-hand side. Well, let's leave the angle of 4 degrees. The angle of 80 degrees, does that appear as if the shot was fired almost at a right angle in relation to the tram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we only look at that piece of information, then yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have -- well, this page can stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like you to look at the previous paragraph, which states that: "The entry point of the first bullet in the tin is located in the metal of the back part of the tram, right outside side, 84.5 centimetres from the center of the tram and 153.5 centimetres inside the tram." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how thick is the wall, the side of the tram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, you are again embarking on technical aspects of this whole matter. I really have no idea how thick the side wall of the tram is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's do it like this: Between 84.5 centimetres, where the bullet entered the wall of the tram, and 6.5 centimetres [as interpreted], the difference between those two measurements is 18 centimetres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in simple calculation, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this does not appear to be a perpendicular angle, but a very sloped angle. So no matter what the thickness of the wall of the tram was, the bullet would be travelling through the wall of the tram for 18 centimetres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really am unable to -- I'm a serious man. I cannot participate in the clarification of this kind; not because I don't want to, but simply because I am not able to follow this terminology. In my practice, when I have a case like this, the things that Dr. Karadzic is talking about are clarified for me and dealt with by my colleagues who are experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You concluded that the bullet came from Metalka, from Grbavica, a building which was under the control of the Serbian forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see again my official report so that I could possibly confirm what was just being said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have time for that now. Can we now look at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is it true that the bullet came from Serbian positions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just for the record, could Mr. Karadzic identify where, exactly, the witness said it came from the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you withdraw that question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is definitely stated somewhere in the investigation documents. I don't know if that is in his part of the report. I'm talking about the whole report, and this witness was the team leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you refer to the exact page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're looking for this: Mr. Miokovic, you said that the bullet came from Serbian positions. Which part of the Serbian positions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I will kindly request that my official report be placed on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your part of the report, it says "from Grbavica." Did you not conclude that the bullet came from Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 6 in B/C/S and 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still don't see my report in front of me. I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The automatic weapons from the aggressors' positions --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we look at the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not see where Mr. Karadzic was reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It should be the previous page, first paragraph: "On the 3rd of March, this centre was informed ..." That was information he received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this information confirmed in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official report that I drafted, in general, as well as the one we see before us here, I've already explained the methodology of preparing these reports. And I stress, and I will do it again, each technical detail, such as it had come from Grbavica, and what type of weapon, that is something that I enter in my report as a preliminary information. And then ballistics experts and forensic technicians prepare their own reports within a time-frame assigned, and those reports contain the full information, and they are, as such, forwarded to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have 1D2433.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. While we're waiting for the document to come up, I just wanted to indicate I would ask the Court for two minutes at the end of the session to address one scheduling matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark on this photograph, going from left to right, the site where you found the tram? First of all, let's do that. The exact point.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. In other words, the tram was moving from the new to the old part of town. I don't have the report before me. Can you just help me and tell me, was the tram moving from the old to the new -- from the new to the old part, or the other way around?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's correct, from the new part of town to the old part, from west to east.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you found it -- where you found it, it was at Marin Dvor. Could you please mark that location on the photograph here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not easy to find my bearings, but I think it's about here somewhere [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please mark the old tobacco factory.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The premises of the old tobacco factory?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what you mean. I lived in Sarajevo for 50 years, but I've never heard of the old tobacco factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you then please mark the Vrbanja Bridge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please put "1" next to the tram stop at Marin Dvor and "2" at the Vrbanja Bridge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now please put the number 3 on the Executive Council building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 4 for the Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now please draw a line through Djure Danicica Street, as it was called in the past, which runs --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the directions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you want me to mark that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, just draw a line through it, and please put the number 5 next to it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And would you now please mark the Franje Rackog Street, all the way to the Holiday Inn, or, rather, to the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that what we see perpendicular to the tram tracks, that that is an articulated tram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please put the number 7 there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then on the right-hand track --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't see. Can you help me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it lies across the road.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, I can see it now [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would we agree now that this tram that we see at number 8, that it is moving from the Stari to Novi Grad, from the old part of town to the new part of town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now please mark the spot where your investigative team determined that the tram was impacted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my official report, it says that the round had come from Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, for the transcript, would you please say the right-hand tram -- number 8, it's moving from the new to the old part of town. I just want to say that for the transcript. Now, first, mark the spot where your team determined that the tram received the bullet.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, I think it was the corner of Zmaja od Bosne and Franje Rackog Street. It is approximately in this area here. I'll mark it now [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where had the round come from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you determine the direction and the place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put number 9, for the record, for the place of incident.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please just confirm whether the tram, marked with number 8, is moving from the new part of town to the old part of town, from Novi Grad to Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can confirm that that is, in fact, the track leading from the old -- the new part of town to the old part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark the tram that has not yet entered the curve.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't see that tram that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, is the tram that is about to enter the place which you marked with a circle number 9; can you see it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please the number 10 there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, could we put, either on this photo or on a new one -- could you indicate the trajectory -- the trajectory -- the bullet trajectory and the position from which it came? Perhaps you can use the red pen and we can mark the trajectory on this same photo.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I can do is draw a line with an arrow indicating the direction from Grbavica to the spot where the tram was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this bullet was supposed to hit the tram, flying over the museum building; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, tell us, where the red line begins, is that the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the building that several witnesses have confirmed to be the Metalka building, but never mind. Would you please date and sign this photo.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's time to take a break, Mr. Karadzic. We'll admit it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D846, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next witness, I wanted to note, has actually been here since Sunday, mainly to accommodate the accused's request to participate in an interview. We anticipated that we would begin his testimony on Thursday, based on the projected schedule. Clearly, we won't begin until today. I wanted, however, to inquire, particularly in light of the witness's co-operation and accommodation, if we could do the same for him and if there was a possibility of an additional session today. I note that a courtroom is available. I appreciate the logistical issues involved, but I would ask the Court to consider the possibility of an additional session, for example, from 2.30 to 4.30, to maximise the prospect of concluding this witness's evidence, if not today, at least first thing on Monday, before the videolinks. If the Court needs any additional information, I'm happy to provide it, but I think you understand the situation, and it would be extremely helpful if we could implement measures that would maximise the prospect of concluding this witness's -- the next witness's testimony at the earliest possible moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll consider the matter. But, Mr. Karadzic, after the session you will have about 15 minutes to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case, many of the incidents will remain unclarified. I will not be able to explore them with this witness. And I do acknowledge that there is a certain responsibility on my part for not being efficient enough, but I will not be able to examine all these incidents. The team leader of an investigating team has to be aware of the information. He has to know the explanations for certain things. So who else can I examine these issues with, if not with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I told you, you had to prioritise your questions and not to waste your time. After having wasted a lot of time, asking for an extension is unacceptable. The Chamber will discuss your request for extension of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just address you with one final issue. Can I ask the following: Whatever I fail or am unable to cover, no matter how efficient I am, and even if I do prioritise it, can whatever was left out of what I was able to check, can that be the basis for a conviction? If that is the case, then there should be no prioritisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Half an hour. We'll resume at 12.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you will have half an hour to conclude your cross-examination. And thanks to the indulgence of all the staff involved, I'm pleased to inform you that we can go until 3.00 this afternoon, albeit we may have a short break in the meantime. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, who is Enes Bezdrob?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enes Bezdrob was a police employee who, at a certain period of time during the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sarajevo, was chief of Security Service of CSB Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, I hope that when I say "you," and by that I mean the BH Army, I hope this is not irritating you. Therefore, do not refer to what we did as an aggression.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreter couldn't hear your question. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question was whether Enes Bezdrob was the chief of the centre during the time that this incident that we are dealing with took place.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember, he was the chief of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have again 1D2433.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the end of the street that used to be called Titova Street?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this is the end or the beginning, but I think it's somewhere here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please now draw a straight line along the middle of the tram, which is here, so extend it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parallel with the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, you can do it through the tram, itself.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you do the same with the tram which is positioned before the S-curve.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please just put number 1 where you think Titova Street ends.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't think it's clear enough.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now it's okay. Now, Mr. Miokovic, I'm going to put to you what is contained in the report by the team that you headed and under whose leadership they operated. The report says that the bullet came from above, from the right, and travelled downwards to the left from the back side to the front side. So this is what is said in the report, that the bullet came from the back side of the tram, travelled towards the front end of the tram, downwards to the left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember having read this a minute ago, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the same time, it was established and determined that the angle of trajectory had an angle with the axis of the tram of 80 degrees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the ballistic report says, the one that I read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please put the date and your signature on this picture.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, according to the axes of these trams, can you use them as a benchmark and draw an angle of 80 degrees, which would indicate the incoming trajectory towards the tram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not able to draw that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's simple geography. This is not ballistics. But, anyway, can we have this document admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D847.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 10439, page 4. Well, let's keep this image for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please now mark the spot where you conducted your on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I now ask you to draw a straight line from the top of the building of the Executive Council, from both tops, to the tram.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which ones do you mean; the one closer to the tram stop?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From both north and south, from which one can see the tram stop.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] So this is from the Executive Council building. That's number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then from the southern corner of the Executive Council building.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you also please date and sign this photograph.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 10439, page 4. Has this image been admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was about to say that asking the witness to draw meaningless lines is unhelpful. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D848, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have page 4 that I asked for, 10439.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document. Was it signed by Enes Bezdrob, the chief of the centre, on the 4th of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document that I see in front of me is a dispatch, and earlier I explained what this means. And as a rule of service, all the dispatches were signed by Enes Bezdrob.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see here that in paragraph 3, the site location was determined as being at the intersection of Marsala Tita Street and Franje Rackog Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is this already in evidence? If not, can we tender it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's already admitted as part of P1727.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have -- can we now have 1D2673. Once again, I am not going to throw you into any ballistic discussions, but we will deal with simple geometry that is being taught in elementary schools.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, in your report with respect to the articulated part of the tram, the difference between the entry and exit wound is 18 centimetres or 180 millimetres; is that correct? From 84.5 to 66.5 centimetres, the balance is 18 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have my report in front of me, but to the best of my recollection, that is what is written there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I think we're heading down -- despite what Mr. Karadzic said, we're going straight into the area of ballistics, which this witness has said repeatedly he is not -- it was not his area. And, also, the expression "entry and exit wound" might be intended to read "entry and exit point" in the question, in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I didn't follow, for myself, how we could come to the number of 18 centimetres when he asked the question. The witness didn't confirm it entirely with you. I agree with Mr. Gaynor. Move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It's not entry and exit wound, it's entry and exit point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, in the report signed by Mr. Miokovic, it is stated that the external entry point is 84.5 centimetres above the articulated part and that the exit point is at 66.5 centimetres. You can apply simple arithmetic, and get 18 centimetres, which means that the bullet travelled through the wall of the tram along the line of 18 centimetres. It's clear to everyone, and the witness confirmed that these entry and exit holes were at these dimensions. This is simple arithmetic and geometry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, do you agree if --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please slow down. It is impossible to follow all these figures and numbers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm sorry, Mr. Miokovic. The interpreters couldn't hear you because you are too fast. But I told you to move on to another topic. You can discuss it with your expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, these are matters which are contained in the report and can be contested by -- either contested or confirmed by an expert witness later. As I understand this, these are not an original analysis by this witness, anyway, but simply a repetition of findings by others.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is simply a visualisation of the figures contained in this witness's report. The figures were accepted. I just wanted to present this visually. Can we again have document 1D2433.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, do you agree -- or do we agree that between Grbavica and the tram track, at any point represented in this picture are the buildings that were being used by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never became familiarised precisely with the positions of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, what I know and what I'm certain about is that Vilsonovo Setaliste and the River Miljacka were practically no-man's land and that practically that was the separation line between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you accept that the buildings, such as the museum -- both museums, actually, the Faculty of Philosophy, the Assembly building, the Government building, Unis skyscraper, the technical school, were being used by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, and I cannot confirm your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who controlled this area that I described? Was it the Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the angles stated in your report, did you investigate the possibility of the bullet coming from any of those buildings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This type of analysis, as far as I know, was not carried out. However, I would like to reiterate that this particular investigation was led by the investigating judge and not by me. So if the investigating judge gave such an order to the ballistic experts to do so, then it was done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me confirm about the 18 centimetres you raised. Can you bring up page 9 of the Exhibit P1727. I mean the English page. And I also refer to the transcript page, page 59, line 5 to 8. Yes. Is there a misinterpretation, a typo, in the English translation? It says "84.5 centimetres from center of the train," and later on, "6.5 centimetres from the center of the tram," and you come to 18 centimetres. I didn't understand that right. The transcript reads like --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the original, it says "66.5."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I didn't follow it at the time. In any event, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in your report, it says "66.5"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I kindly ask to have a look at my report on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we have it here on this side. It says: "The damage on the external part of the tram, between the --" [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask to look at the text on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a criminal investigation technician report, and I confirm that it is written just the way you have read.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not the same page, I take it. Can we see the report written by Medjedovic. It's probably page 7 or 8 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think Mr. Medjedovic's report is at about page 17 in B/C/S. This is the report that Mr. Karadzic has been presenting as Mr. Miokovic's report, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Miokovic was the leader of that team, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to notice "66.5, left side of the tram." Thank you. It's hidden from the end of the frame. Yes, "66.5." Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now deal with the sniper incident number 14 from the List F, the incident that took place on the 23rd of November, 1994. Did you take part in the investigation of that incident?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seem to remember so, but I would kindly ask to have my official report on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 09699, page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit 1714, P1714.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you the leader of the team in this investigation as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This investigation was also headed by the investigating judge, and by that very fact, I was somebody who was acting under his instructions. This investigation was headed by a judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you need to look or can you briefly tell us what happened and what you concluded? What was your final conclusion? Can I recommend the first passage to you after the names. Is it correct that you did not carry out the on-scene investigation but that you did this in the garage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of what is written here, absolutely, yes. Obviously, in this situation, we did not perform the investigation at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And would this be important for the purposes of establishing, down to the metre, the precise position of the tram when it was impacted by the bullet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In each kind of ballistics expertise, this is something that is exceptionally important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And here, nevertheless, the investigation of the tram is being carried out at the garage, in the depot, and the position is taken that the bullet had come from Serbian positions; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it states here that the tram was hit with one bullet of an undetermined calibre, which fragmented, due to which two bullet traces were left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to tell us what the consequences were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, and I can see that here, that two females were wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at 1D2415. Is this -- this is probably part of the exhibit, this thing, P17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you able to mark, on this Google Maps photograph, the location that you were told where the tram was when it was hit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to read from my report, if you have it in front of you, what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it now. It says that you -- the duty officers informed you that from the aggressor's position from Grbavica, and so on and so forth, was fired, and that the tram was hit in the section between the technical school and the Marsal Tito Barracks and Zmaja od Bosne Street. The tram was hit in the area of its middle section; more precisely, a little bit in front of the articulated part. The shot was fired from the south/south-west, isn't it -- south-east -- south/south-east, and this was at the turning towards Nova Stanica. Are you able to mark here the turning to the Nova Stanica? Are you able to mark the technical school here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just trying to orient myself here. This is the technical school, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't it this black square part that is a bit to the west in relation to the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. I made a mistake. Yes, yes, I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please, then, circle the building where the technical school was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Wait a minute, Mr. Miokovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the Marsal Tito Barracks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can only see a part of it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it with the number 2?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you please now mark the trams that are going from the S-curve to the Nova Stanica. You can mark the tracks along their length, and can that be number 3?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you now mark the place where the tram was when it was hit and what was its position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you again: In my report, did you say that was in this part of the tram that leads to the new railway station?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah, and you don't remember that, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I did many of such investigations at the scene, and they are all more or less similar. Or you can just call up my report on the screen, and after that I will be able to mark the location of the tram precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then we would lose -- well, I would like it to be given to you. You can have my copy of the hard copy of your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Then maybe in the meantime I'll read out the passage. It says: "The tram was hit in --" forgive my pronunciation -- "in Zmaja od Bosne Street, between tehnicka skola," I take it "technical school," "and the KMT. It was hit in the center, more precisely, near the connecting platform. The bullet was fired from south or south-east." You have that report with you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will mark it with the number 4 [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Had the tram already turned towards the station? More specifically, what was the position of its horizontal axis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I don't see anywhere in my official report that the tram was turning towards the new railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it says here that it was at the S-curve.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that is why -- this is the S-curve. There is the right-hand part of the tram tracks going to the new railway station, and on the other side it's going towards the new part of town. So I don't see that, at the point when the tram was hit, that it was about to turn north towards the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to indicate on this picture where the south-east is, one long, straight line indicating the south-east?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to the tram position?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, in relation to the point marked with the number 4, where the tram was hit. That is the direction that is stated, and you can extend the line a little further, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we mark this now with the number 5?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is the direction -- that is one of the directions that is indicated in the report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know where the line of separation is located here on the left bank of the Miljacka River?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it's from the Vrbanja Bridge towards the west. The entire left bank was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to mark the building of Unioninvest, which is now the building of the High Representative? And you can mark that building with the number 6.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to try, but I would also ask you to follow on the screen [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In relation to Vrbanja, you will remember where it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark that with the number 6.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, who had that building in their hands?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that that building in the Ljubljanska Street was -- actually, that the lines between the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army and the Bosnian Serb Army was not always a constant straight line, so things changed. So I don't know at the time who had control of this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that right from the beginning of 1992, that building was under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, would that be acceptable to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that I can reply to that, with all due respect, is that I cannot accept that assertion of yours for one simple reason, and that reason is that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. Fair enough. And now, please, were any measurements taken on the tram, itself; height measurements and the relational measurements along the vertical and the horizontal lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to my experience, that is the main task of my colleagues, technicians from the Criminal Investigation Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And were the measurements given in the report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These measures should have been quoted in that report, and that report should have been a part of this file. It should have accompanied my official report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we ask the Prosecution, my learned friend Mr. Gaynor, to help us to find, in material that he has, whether this report exists?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now it's time for you to wrap up your cross-examination. Could you kindly put the date and your signature on this marked picture, and we'll admit it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit D849.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellencies. Mr. Miokovic was working, especially on the 1st of July, on some incidents, but today we don't have time. I kindly ask for the support of the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution so that we can get all the reports of all the investigative actions in which Mr. Miokovic took part, if the Prosecution has them. If not, we can request them from the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have re-examination, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I do, yes, have a few minutes of re-examination. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The first subject concerns the sequence of events on the 8th of November, 1994. Mr. Karadzic was asking you a few questions about the time of your arrival at the site of the first impact, the time of your departure, and the time of your return after the second and third shells came. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, did you, on Wednesday, with my assistance, create a short summary of the sequence of events on the afternoon of the 8th of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask for 65 ter 90199, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is that the short summary which you had an opportunity to review?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the short summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You had an opportunity to make corrections to this, and, in fact, you did make corrections; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is that your signature that appears at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed that on the 27th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And that is an accurate summary of the events of the afternoon of the 8th of November, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender that for admission, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1850, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The next subject I'd like to turn to is: On the next day, the 9th of November, 1994, Mr. Karadzic was making the point that the investigative judge on that day was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you remember him referring to that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in your report of the incident, which is P1706 -- no need to bring it up unless you want to see it, but you list the participation of the expert ballistics member of your team, who is Zlatko Medjedovic. You know that man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately, I knew him. I say "unfortunately" because he passed away in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you happen to know his ethnic background, what his ethnic background was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, is that the same Mr. Medjedovic who is referred to as the ballistics expert in your reports concerning the other -- the sniping incident of the 3rd of March, 1995, and the sniping incident of the 24th of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Earlier on today, Mr. Karadzic showed you a report dated the 3rd of March, 1995, prepared by Mihajlo Pavlovic. Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you happen to know his ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mihajlo is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I address you briefly with a question or short explanation? Namely, I do not attach any importance to ethnic background of any expert or government officials, but it was Mr. Gaynor who introduced this topic from Day 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your intervention is not helpful, Mr. Karadzic. Judge Lattanzi has a question for you, Mr. Miokovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I need some clarification from you regarding your relationship with the UNPROFOR. This morning, during cross-examination, it appeared, regarding a specific incident, I think the one in Livanjska Ulica, but I'm not just referring to that incident because you presented the question as being general, you mentioned some misunderstanding or lack of understanding with UNPROFOR, so when you were investigating during on-site investigation. That's what you mentioned. I wanted to know whether there was an agreement between the UN and the BiH Presidency or Government as to the procedure to be followed during on-site investigations with regard to UN personnel participation or even for independent on-site investigation. So I was wondering whether you were aware of such specific procedures. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, there were procedures, and now I'm talking about the Security Services Centre of Sarajevo, of which I was a member, in relation to UNPROFOR forces deployed in the Sarajevo canton. Now, concerning investigations -- on-site investigations of this and similar incidents, the police of the CSB of Sarajevo canton and its investigating organs, by which I mean investigating judge, were completely independent, professionally speaking. In professional terms and in terms of legal provisions that were in force in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time, the position of UNPROFOR was not specified precisely by any means. Let me be quite clear. Anything that was determined during an on-site investigation is something that the local investigating team takes responsibility for. In view of the situation prevailing at the time, I'm just limiting myself to the area of Sarajevo. The interest, if you wish, of the Presidency and the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time was to have everything relating to incidents of this nature be completely transparent. So in the majority of cases and in principle, and the investigations that I was personally involved in, certainly 90 per cent of them were attended by representatives of UNPROFOR who, in most cases when they were present, again in 90 per cent of such cases, practically did nothing. They were just standing there and supervised, in a manner, the operations that we carried out. As much as I would like, I cannot remember a single on-site investigation that I carried out of this type when UNPROFOR requested that they carry out their separate investigation and that reconstruction was requested. So we had very clear-cut relationships with them. In practice, there were instances, prior to the meeting mentioned by Dr. Karadzic, that UNPROFOR, due to the fact that their technical capabilities, in terms of the vehicles they had, and the possibility of their moving through the town during shelling or some other safety hazard, would arrive on the crime scene before us. I have no reason to doubt that, vertically hierarchically, the UNPROFOR had their guide-lines and instructions as to how to conduct themselves during on-site investigations. There were some instances when, I must say that, UNPROFOR representatives did not conduct themselves in an appropriate manner. They would come before us to the site, I don't know why, and then they would simply collect all the relevant evidence. For example, if we had a shelling incident, they would take all the fragments of the explosive device, which made it virtually impossible for us to carry out an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To understand it properly, to sum it up, the UNPROFOR was entitled to take part in on-site investigation carried out by you, but they were not entitled to conduct independent on-site investigations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the right to conduct independent investigations. We never wanted or did dispute that. However, according to the procedure laid down by our law, that could not be considered a relevant part of the investigation relating to a specific incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to -- thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. Before we start again with the next witness, we'll have a short break for 10 minutes, and we'll resume at quarter to 2:00 clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 1.36 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Brennskag. If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, could you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG
utterances.text: Per Anton Brennskag.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You gave statements to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in May 1996 and October 2006; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You testified here on two previous occasions, and that was in the trials of Dragomir Milosevic and -- in March 2007 and in Momcilo Perisic in February 2009; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On Tuesday, the 26th of October, you had an opportunity to review and sign an amalgamated statement which contains relevant parts from your earlier statements, testimony, and information provided to the OTP. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I ask for 65 ter 90195, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Brennskag, on the screen in front of you, do you recognise that which bears your signature, an electronic copy of the first page of your amalgamated statement which you indicated you had an opportunity to review?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does that statement accurately reflect your previous statements and testimony, or, in fact, those portions of the previous statements and testimonies which have been put into this statement?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you were examined in court today on the same subjects, would you provide the same information to the Court in response to those questions?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender for admission 65 ter 90195, the amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
